- When sentiment is positive (≥0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.3), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 3–7% for next 3–7 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak for 3–5 days.  
- If model forecast is consistently >10% above recent 18-day average, apply mean reversion: subtract 1–3% per day until closer to historical range.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows early sharp decline (first 5–7 days), model often fails to anticipate; reduce first 5 days’ forecast by 5–10%.  
- If sentiment history shows no clear trend (all 0.00), model tends to be overly conservative; add 2–4% to forecast for next 7 days.
